title: When may a phase gate cross a permutation?
assumptions: Let \(X\) be a finite nonempty set with orthonormal basis \(\{|x\rangle:x\in X\}\). For a permutation \(p\) of \(X\) and a function \(a:X\to\mathbb T\), write \(M(a,p)|x\rangle=a(x)|p(x)\rangle\), where \(\mathbb T=\{z\in\mathbb C:|z|=1\}\).
Write \(P_p=M(1,p)\) for pure routing and \(D_f=M(f,\mathrm{id})\) for a phase table \(f:X\to\mathbb T\).
conventions: Kets are columns. The rightmost factor acts first. Rows label outputs, and columns label inputs. Two operators agree up to global phase when one is a single constant of modulus one times the other on all inputs.
question:
Determine the output label and amplitude of \(M(b,q)M(a,p)|x\rangle\) for arbitrary weights and permutations. A circuit designer wants to move a phase gate to the input side of a routing gate. Determine the unique table \(g\) satisfying \(D_fP_p=P_pD_g\). When does keeping the original table give exact equality? When does keeping it give equality up to a single global phase? Prove both tests.

As a wiring check, let \(X=\{0,1\}^2\), write a label as \((c,t)\) with control bit first, and take \(p(c,t)=(c,t\mathbin{\oplus}c)\) and \(f(c,t)=e^{i\theta t}\) for real \(\theta\). Give the corrected input-side table and determine every angle for which the uncorrected reordering is valid, both exactly and up to a global phase. At \(\theta=\pi\), give a normalized two-term input for which the two uncorrected orderings produce orthogonal states, even though their computational-basis output probabilities agree on each computational-basis input.
